reason: E1 directly supports that rapid quenching produces an amorphous structure and slow cooling yields crystalline phases, and it mentions enhanced glass-forming ability from phosphorus and entropy. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that the amorphous state has higher thermal stability (elevated crystallization onset) than the slow-cooled baseline, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 yields an amorphous structure
Slow cooling of the same alloy produces a complex crystalline microstructure
The amorphous structure from rapid quenching exhibits higher thermal stability (elevated crystallization onset) than the slow-cooled crystalline state
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass-forming ability in this alloy system
